tessa: FYI I pushed a tiny proposal to simplify the WeightLoadingBridge surface. TL;DR: split IO vs orchestration, deprecate dual-role methods, add a thin compatibility shim for existing safetensors manifests.

rick: quick Q — when you say 'IO vs orchestration' do you mean the Loader should only be responsible for byte access + validation, and Bridge just composes loaders into a warmup plan? or is Bridge still doing some index-first heuristics?

janet: exactly. Loader -> read chunks, validate checksums, expose a small iterator API. Bridge/Coordinator -> decide chunk order, prefetch priorities, eviction hints. Makes testing and mocking way easier.

miguel: big +1 for separation, but streaming workloads worry me. If loader is dumb IO-only, who handles partial-shard streaming and backpressure? we don't want to reintroduce head-of-line blocking by putting too much logic in the coordinator. :thinking:

warmup-bot: deploybot: build succeeded for branch weight-bridge-refactor (ci/eng-ml#2345) :white_check_mark:

tessa: good point @miguel. Proposal is to keep a small 'streaming-adapter' concept inside the Loader API (opt-in). Loader defaults to random-access chunk reads but can also implement a streaming iterator that yields (chunk_id, ready_future) and a backpressure callback. Bridge still makes high-level ordering decisions but must respect loader backpressure signals.

rick: sounds flexible. What about indexing-first vs manifestless streaming? We have customers on both extremes. Any plan for fallbacks?

janet: compatibility shim maps manifest-first and manifestless formats into a uniform 'ShardDescriptor' model. For index-first we expose precise byte ranges. For manifestless/stream-first we return a live descriptor with expected total size and per-chunk progressive checksums. Bridge treats both as the same contract. This is the lightweight shim I mentioned.

miguel: performance tradeoff: index-first lets us do parallel random access and prioritize hot layers. stream-first benefits cold starts where index generation is expensive. We should document expected latencies and recommend index-first for Dedicated/DC customers and streaming for Hosted scenarios.

tessa: agreed. Also adding a small heuristics table to the spec: when model_size > X and mean_seq_length < Y => prefer index-first. We'll shove that into Optimize as a recommendation and surface it in the Console (per-route suggestions).

rick: impl detail — deprecating existing Bridge methods will break older Dedicated agents. Plan to release shim in two phases: 1) runtime accepts both APIs, logs deprecation, 2) remove after N months. The shim will live in inflight adapters module.

janet: +1. Also add a feature gate for "loader_streaming_adapter" so we can roll canary Traffic.

miguel: one more: eviction interplay. If Bridge schedules warmup for a shard but eviction runs mid-warmup, we need an atomic lease or checkpoint to avoid double-warmup storms. Proposal: warmup coordinator obtains a short-lived 'hydrate lease' on shard_id which is checked by eviction. Lease grants 60s soft hold, renewables while active. Thoughts?

tessa: that fixes a lot of races. Keep lease semantics minimal: holder id + expiry + optional priority token. Eviction checks for active lease and either delays or steals based on priority. We'll draft a lease RFC.

rick: can we also emit telemetry hooks for lease churn? want to see warmup storms in prod quickly.

janet: yes — emit events: lease_acquired, lease_renewed, lease_released, lease_stolen with metadata. Connect them to rollout alerts.

miguel: sample shim/interface I sketched in code (inline):

```
# Loader minimal interface
class Loader:
    def open(self) -> None: pass
    def read_chunk(self, chunk_id: str) -> bytes: pass
    def stream_chunks(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[str, Future[bytes]]]: pass
    def validate_header(self) -> HeaderMeta

# Coordinator/Bridge uses ShardDescriptor
ShardDescriptor = {
    'shard_id': str,
    'chunks': List[str],
    'index_available': bool,
}
```

miguel: this is purposely tiny. We keep heavy heuristics out of Loader.

tessa: perfect. I'll convert this into the branch patch and a short RFC note for the eng-ml channel. Plan: land shim + feature gate, enable canary for internal infra, collect lease telemetry, then ramp.

rick: thanks — if we can also include a short migration checklist for Dedicated agents (what flags to flip, how to reason about streaming vs index mode) that'd be helpful.

janet: I'll draft the checklist and ping infra team for canary hosts.

miguel: :shipit:
